narrative:
The model estimated a 51.1% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is just over even odds, but it crossed the risk threshold used for admission, so your application was denied. This is a probability-based warning, not a determination that you cannot pass.

The denial was driven mainly by your third-year rank in your school: you were in the second decile, compared with an average of about 5.8 among accepted students. This was the strongest factor and pushed the prediction toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 was the second most influential factor; it was slightly above the accepted-student average of 3.23 and pushed toward passing. Your LSAT was the third most influential factor and also leaned toward passing, though it was not strong enough to outweigh the third-year rank signal.

To strengthen a future application, focus on showing improved upper-level academic performance, consider whether a higher LSAT score is realistic, and seek admissions or pre-law advising on how to present grade trends and any extenuating circumstances. Ask the school for feedback and apply to programs that review the full record rather than a single predictive score.
